content.body:
After 15 years as a dermatologist, I watched Sarah sit in my office crying.

She'd spent two years trying to stop her hair falling out. Tried biotin. Tried collagen. Tried every expensive shampoo she could find.

Her doctor ran blood tests. Everything came back normal.

But her hair kept falling out in clumps.

I finally asked her the one question nobody else had:

"When was the last time someone checked your ferritin?"

She looked at me like I was speaking another language.

My name is Dr. Emma Chen. I'm a board-certified dermatologist and I've treated over 8,000 women with hair loss.

And here's what most doctors miss.

Sarah was 34. Healthy. Doing everything "right."

But her hair was falling out in clumps. Every morning. Clumps in the drain. Clumps on her brush. Her ponytail used to be thick. Now she could wrap her fingers around it twice. She'd stopped wearing it down because she could see her scalp.

And she was exhausted. The kind of tired where your whole body feels like cement. Crashing by 2pm. Coffee doing nothing.

Her doctor checked her iron. Said it was normal.

But she never checked her ferritin — her iron storage. That's a completely different number.

I tested it. The result came back: 13.

Normal range technically starts at 12. But hair needs ferritin above 70 to grow properly.

Sarah's hair wasn't falling out because of stress. It wasn't genetics.

Her hair was starving. And nobody had checked.

When ferritin drops too low, your body goes into survival mode. Your heart needs iron. Your brain needs iron.

Your hair? Not essential.

So your body steals iron from your follicles to keep you alive. That's why the shedding won't stop. That's why you're exhausted. Same cause.

I started testing ferritin on every woman who came in with hair loss.

Over twelve months, I tested 214 women. 187 had ferritin below 50.

87%.

All had been told they were "fine."

But here's where it gets worse.

Most iron supplements don't fix it.

Ferrous sulfate — the cheap kind doctors prescribe — only absorbs at 15%. The rest wrecks your stomach. Constipation. Nausea. And your ferritin barely moves.

Liquid iron — gentler, but doses are tiny. Women take it for months and their levels go up 3 points.

I saw it constantly. Women trying iron, getting sick or seeing no results, giving up. Hair still falling out.

Then I discovered why.

Iron bisglycinate absorbs 4x better with no stomach issues. But it needs vitamin C, B6 and B12 alongside it — otherwise your body can't store it as ferritin.

Most supplements have one or the other. Almost none have everything.

I spent weeks looking for something I could actually recommend.

That's when I found FerraVital.

Chelated iron bisglycinate. Vitamin C. B6. B12. Even wholefood beetroot iron. Everything the research says is needed. Nothing unnecessary.

I started recommending it to patients whose ferritin was stuck. The women who'd tried everything. The women who couldn't tolerate other iron.

Sarah was one of the first.

Week 4: The afternoon crashes stopped. She had energy past 2pm for the first time in years.

Week 6: The shedding slowed. She washed her hair and didn't see clumps in the drain. She wasn't terrified to brush it anymore.

Week 8: Baby hairs. Tiny ones at first, around her hairline. Then more.

Week 12: We tested again. Ferritin was 74.

Thirteen to seventy-four in twelve weeks.

She sat in my office and cried again. But different this time.

"I feel like myself again. I actually recognise myself."

I've now recommended FerraVital to over 400 women.

Michelle, 38: "My ferritin went from 16 to 71. My hair finally stopped falling out after two years."

Jessica, 42: "I'd given up on iron because it destroyed my stomach. This one didn't. My hair is thicker than it's been in years."

Rebecca, 29: "Three doctors told me it was stress. My ferritin was 11. Nobody checked."

The pattern is always the same.

Dismissed. Told they were fine. Watched their hair fall out and blamed themselves.

If your hair is falling out and you're exhausted all the time — your ferritin is probably in the teens.

That's not normal. That's not stress. That's not ageing.

Your hair is starving.

Don't wait until you can see your scalp.

Don't wait until you've cried more this year than the last five combined.

Don't wait until you don't recognise yourself anymore.

Link's below if you want to check it out.

content.body:
I was exhausted all the time and my hair was falling out in clumps.

I dreaded washing it. Every single time. Because I knew what was coming. Clumps in the drain. Clumps on my brush. Hair everywhere.

My ponytail used to be so thick. Now I could wrap my fingers around it twice. I started avoiding mirrors. Stopped wearing it down because I could see my scalp. I didn't even recognise myself anymore.

And the tiredness — god, the tiredness. My whole body felt like it was weighted down with cement. I'd wake up exhausted. Crash by 2pm. Coffee stopped doing anything months ago.

I thought I was just lazy. That something was just wrong with me.

I went to my doctor. She ran the standard blood tests. Told me my iron was ‘normal’.

But I knew something wasn't right. You don't lose hair like this and feel this tired for no reason.

So I paid for a private blood test myself. 

Turns out my ferritin (iron store) was 13. Thirteen.

My doctor still tried to call that "within normal range." 

But I looked it up — hair needs ferritin at 70 to actually grow. My hair was literally starving.

I tried to fix it on my own.

Ferrous sulfate first. The $15 one off Amazon that doctors always prescribe. It wrecked my stomach. Constipation. Nausea so bad I couldn't focus on work. And my hair? Still falling out.
Then I tried Floradix liquid iron. It didn't destroy my stomach like the pills. But I took it for months and my ferritin didn't budge. My hair kept getting thinner.
I stopped looking in mirrors. I couldn't handle watching it disappear.
Then I came across this dermatologist on TikTok talking about how common hair loss from low ferritin is.
She explained why most iron doesn't work. Ferrous sulfate only absorbs at like 15% (explains the constipation and nausea) and liquid iron doses are too small to make a difference.
She said what actually works is chelated iron bisglycinate. Absorbs 4x better with no stomach issues. But it needs to have vitamin C, B6 and B12 alongside it — otherwise your body can't absorb it and store it as ferritin.

So I went looking for something that had all of this.
That's when I found FerraVital.
It had all the ingredients she mentioned plus wholefood beetroot iron. Everything she said made sense. So I gave it one more shot.

Took the capsule every morning on an empty stomach as instructed. 

Week 4: I stopped needing my third cup of coffee. The afternoon crashes started to fade. I actually had energy past 2pm for the first time in years.

Week 6: The shedding slowed down. I washed my hair and didn't see huge clumps in the drain. I wasn't terrified to brush it anymore.

Week 8: Baby hairs. Tiny ones at first, around my hairline. Then more. I kept checking the mirror thinking I was imagining it.

Week 12: I got my levels checked again. Ferritin was 74.
Thirteen to seventy-four in twelve weeks.
My hair is really getting thick now. My energy’s returned. I feel like myself again.
I started reading reviews from other women taking it.
I wasn't alone.
Sarah: "My ferritin went from 11 to 68. My hair finally stopped falling out after two years."
Michelle: "I thought I was just a tired person. Turns out I was depleted. I feel like a completely different woman."
Jessica: "My doctor told me my levels were 'normal' at 18. I took matters into my own hands. Best decision I ever made."
The pattern was the same.
We'd all been dismissed. Told we were fine. Watched our hair fall out and blamed ourselves.
Sometimes I think about those two years.
My hair trying to tell me something was wrong.
Me not understanding.
Thinking I was lazy. Thinking I was broken. Thinking this was just who I was now.
If I'd known about ferritin earlier…
If I'd found something that actually worked sooner…
If I'd stopped trusting doctors who said I was "fine"...
But I can't change the past.
I can only share what I learned.
Your hair isn't falling out because of stress.
You're not exhausted because you're lazy.
You're not "just getting older."
Your body is starving for something. And that iron supplement you're taking? It's not giving you what you need.
Your body is trying to tell you something.
Don't wait until you can see your scalp.
Don't wait until you've cried more this year than the last five combined.
Don't wait until you don't recognise yourself anymore.
The solution exists. It's just not what your doctor has told you.
Link's below if you want to check it out.

content.body:
Living with a ferritin of 8 is like trying to breathe at 14,000 feet. Every single day. Except you're standing at sea level and nobody believes you.

That photo is me standing on top of a 14,000-foot mountain. Thumbs up. Tears streaming behind my goggles.

A year ago I couldn't walk to my car without stopping to catch my breath.

Here's what changed.

At 43, I had to choose between pretending I was fine or admitting that my body was shutting down and nobody could tell me why.

I couldn't do both.

The exhaustion was so bad that every single day I'd spend my mornings:

Gripping the stair railing at work so hard my knuckles turned white because my legs felt like they'd buckle

Sitting in my car during lunch with the seat reclined because I physically could not make it to the break room and back

Pulling clumps of hair off my pillow before my husband woke up so he wouldn't see how bad it was getting

My hairstylist stopped pretending. She put her hands on my shoulders and said: "Hon, you need to see someone about this. This isn't normal."

My doctor looked at my labs for three seconds and said: "Your iron is normal. Maybe try biotin."

My husband stopped suggesting weekend hikes — something we used to do every month — because he knew what my face would look like when he asked.

The face that said: "I want to, but my body won't let me."

My breaking point came at my daughter's field day at school.

Parents were invited to run the three-legged race with their kids.

My daughter grabbed my hand. "Mom, we're gonna win!"

I made it maybe 40 feet.

I had to stop. Bent over. Hands on my knees. Gasping.

Other parents jogged past us. Some of them looked back.

My daughter's face went from excited to confused to embarrassed.

"Mom? Are you okay?"

I lied and said yes.

But I wasn't fine.

I was 43 years old, standing in a field on a perfect Saturday morning, and I couldn't run 40 feet with my daughter without almost passing out.

I watched the other moms laughing, crossing the finish line, picking up their kids.

I couldn't even make it halfway.

That night, after my daughter went to bed, I sat on the bathroom floor pulling another clump of hair from the drain and cried.

Not from the hair loss.

From the realization that this thing — whatever it was — had stolen my ability to be the mom I wanted to be.

My energy. My hair. My weekends with my husband. My confidence. My daughter's face when I couldn't keep up with her.

I looked at my husband sleeping in our bed and thought: "Poor guy has probably given up on having the woman he married back."

The next morning, I made an appointment with my fourth doctor.

Dr. Nguyen. A dermatologist.

My friend Carla from work had insisted: "She's different. She actually listens."

I'd heard that before. But I was desperate.

When Dr. Nguyen walked into the exam room, she didn't open her computer.

She pulled up a chair. Sat down. And said: "Tell me everything."

So I did.

I told her about the three years of getting worse with no explanation. The hair loss accelerating every month. The exhaustion so severe I'd fall asleep in my car during lunch. content.body:
My sister's hair was falling out and she had no idea why.

She's 42. She shouldn't be losing her hair like that.

Something was wrong inside her body. And neither of us knew it.

My sister Sarah used to be the life of every room. The one cracking jokes, planning trips, texting me random memes at midnight.

We grew up with the same thick hair. People always commented on it.

She stopped initiating plans. Stopped texting first. Started canceling on me last minute because she was "too tired."

When we did see each other, she seemed distant. Foggy. Like she was there but not really there.

I'd ask how she was doing and she'd just say "fine, just exhausted" every single time.

I watched her go from the sister I knew to someone I barely recognized.

And some days? I didn't know how to reach her anymore.

She tried everything. Better sleep habits. Vitamins. Cutting back on coffee. Exercise.

She tried biotin for months. Collagen in her smoothies. Even Nutrafol at $88 a bottle.

It was like nothing worked.

Some weeks seemed better. Then she'd text me that another clump came out in the shower and she didn't know what to do anymore.

People kept telling her it was just stress. Just aging. Just hormones.

Even her doctor said her labs were "normal."

But my gut knew something was wrong with my sister.

One night I was scrolling through a Facebook group about hair loss after she'd vented to me again, and I saw a thread about how low ferritin causes hair to fall out even when iron levels test "normal."

I'm not gonna lie… I'd never heard of ferritin. I almost scrolled past.

But I kept reading because these women were describing MY sister to a tee.

The hair falling out in clumps. The exhaustion that sleep didn't fix. The brain fog.

But it wasn't just the hair stuff.

These women started listing other things - feeling freezing all the time, craving ice, feeling like a shell of themselves.

That was Sarah. ALL of it.

I went down a rabbit hole that night.

That's when I saw it: "87% of women with unexplained hair loss have low ferritin. But standard lab ranges say anything above 12 is 'normal' - while hair follicles need 70+ to grow."

I froze. That's a massive gap.

Exhaustion that sleep doesn't fix
Brain fog, can't think straight
Feeling cold all the time
Ice chewing or craving ice
Hair falling out in clumps
"Normal" labs but still symptomatic
Biotin, collagen, Nutrafol didn't help
Irritability and mood changes
Brittle nails
Feeling like a shadow of yourself

Then someone broke it down:

2-3 symptoms? Ferritin is likely too low for hair growth.

4 or more? You're almost certainly running on empty.

I started counting Sarah's symptoms.

Exactly five.

My stomach dropped.

I'd been seeing the signs the whole time. I just didn't know what I was looking at.

She'd been running on empty for years and nobody caught it.

She tried pharmacy iron first. Ferrous sulfate.

I went back to that Facebook group.

Woman after woman had the same experience. The pharmacy iron destroyed their stomachs and barely moved their ferritin.

The ones who got results? They used a different form - iron bisglycinate - that absorbs without the gut issues.

But they all emphasized one thing: you need the cofactors. Vitamin C, B12, B6, folate. That's what actually converts iron into stored ferritin.

I spent that night researching until I found one supplement that had everything: the right iron form plus all the cofactors in one capsule.

I sent Sarah the link that night.

I'm not gonna lie… she didn't think it would work. She'd tried so many things.

But about a week in, something shifted.

She texted me first. Just a random meme like she used to. No reason. Just felt like it.

When I called her, she actually sounded awake. Not that foggy, distant voice I'd gotten used to.

By week two, she said the ice cravings stopped. She didn't even notice until she realized she'd walked past the freezer without thinking about it.

The next time I saw her, I noticed it immediately: she looked ALIVE again. The color was back in her face. She was actually laughing.

And her hair? Still thin, but she showed me the baby hairs coming in at her temples. New growth she hadn't seen in years.

By week three, she planned a girls' night. She initiated. She stayed the whole time. No leaving early because she was "too tired."

I almost cried on the way home.

Because I realized: I got my sister back.

The funny, vibrant woman I thought was disappearing was still there.

She just needed her ferritin tank refilled so her body could rebuild.

Now when she has a hard day, it's just a hard day. Not the crushing exhaustion where she couldn't function.

She's still 42. She still gets tired sometimes.

But it's normal tired - not the "I feel like I'm dying and nobody believes me" tired.

If your sister, mom, friend, or even YOU have been slowly fading... if your gut is screaming that something deeper is going on... if you're seeing 2, 3, or 4 of these symptoms…

It's probably low ferritin starving your body and keeping the real you trapped inside.

So you can't think straight, can't get through the day, can't feel like yourself no matter how hard you try.

I know how this sounds. I'd never heard of ferritin either.

But I wish someone had told us years ago - we could've saved so much time.
